doc.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997

title: Faking his way through high school bands without reading music
summary: He played first clarinet in school bands unable to read, copying the neighbor, with his grandfather praising his sound.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: What about, did you fit into the school band situation?

Not at all. Actually I did fool my high school teacher. I was first clarinet in the concert band and in the marching band, and what else, is there — the orchestra. Couldn’t read a note. Luckily the guy next to me was a great reader.

Yeah. I had a real good sound. In fact my grandfather always referred to it as “the voice.” He always used to say in broken Italian, “you have a-the voice — the sound.” Whatever that meant. In later years I guess I kinda got the message. Because if you hear me play clarinet, I do have some kind of a classical sound in a sense, and I never studied. I mean that was the sound I heard all the time. I discussed this with Buddy DeFranco at one time and he had the same kind of background really, and grew up as a little Italian kid playing the clarinet. But you hear all these Italian marches and all of these clarinet things, and that sound kind of, it’s a classical sound but it’s got a little bit more emotion in it I think. I don’t know. Anyway, I got to the point where if we had received a new piece in school, on the side I’d get the fellow next to me, I’d say, I was looking at it and I’d say I didn’t know what that was. I’d say, “Play that for me.” And he’d play it and then I’d play it and then I’d memorize it and that would be it. So I used to sit there and look at the music but I might as well have been reading a Superman comic book. And I played for two years and
the conductor never knew. Maybe he did know, I don’t know. Now that I’m older I think that guy knew but he wanted me in the band.
He liked your sound so he — yeah.
